sprints.title: EduScan rule — detect ModuleProgress.complete() write-key vs hub data-module mismatch (SUPERSEDED — HEUR-025 already exists)
sprints.notes:
PROPOSED 2026-05-08 after marathon shipped 18 write-key fixes across 4 courses (PIS-7, ethics-it-9, intro-security-1, incubator-1). The bug class is recurrent: presentation files call ModuleProgress.complete(house, key, ...) where `key` does not appear in any hub data-module attribute, so completed-presentation checkmarks never display.

**Detection algorithm (proposed):**
  1. For each hub-style index file (`index.html`, `*-index.html`), extract all `data-module="X"` attributes; build platform-wide hubKeys set.
  2. For each `*.presentation.html` file, extract the second argument of any `ModuleProgress.complete()` call.
  3. If the write-key is NOT in the hubKeys set:
     - Check filename-stem alternates (stem, stem+'-pres', stem-suffix removal) in hubKeys. If any matches, flag HUB-002 high (real bug — presentation orphaned from its hub).
     - If no near-match found, classify as orphan (no hub references this content via data-module). Suggest manual triage.

**Severity:**
  - HIGH if a near-match in hubKeys is found (real bug pattern; same class as QC-47/QC-61/QC-46-sub).
  - MEDIUM if presentation is referenced by hub via href anchor but no data-module (unclear intent — may be by design).
  - INFO for true orphans (no hub link at all — likely deprecated content).

**Validator file location**: `_tools/eduscan/validators/syntax/heuristics.js` (extend `checkHubProgressKeyAlignment` or similar new function). Cross-file scan; needs to load all index.html files in a single pass.

**Reference data** (today's marathon — what HUB-002 would have caught at scan time, for free):
  - 7 PIS write-key bugs (commit c4d5bd5e)
  - 9 ethics-it write-key bugs (commit 5efdc9e7)
  - 2 shield write-key bugs (commit 6474259f)
  - These showed up as student-facing bugs months in production before QC-47 surfaced them by accident.

**Build steps:**
  1. Design pro/con + Nancy review (architectural decision: cross-file scan in single-file-validator harness).
  2. Implement validator function with HIGH/MEDIUM/INFO severity tiers.
  3. Run against current platform; expect 0 HIGH (all known instances fixed today), some MEDIUM/INFO.
  4. Smoke gate via deploy.sh — verifies no false positives on shipping content.
  5. Add HUB-002 to TREASURE_MAP severity tracking.

**Pairs with**: HUB-001 (data-module → catalog ID resolution, already exists). HUB-002 covers a different gap — write-key → hub-display alignment.

**Why high priority**: Cheap to build (~50 lines of validator logic). Massive prevention payoff (would catch the entire class of bug we just spent 2h investigating + fixing). Self-healing pipeline can auto-flag future regressions.

--- 2026-05-08 SUPERSEDED ---

HEUR-025 (Module completion ID mismatch) ALREADY EXISTS at `_tools/eduscan/validators/syntax/heuristics.js:2371`. Same scope: data-module + href pair detection (Strategy 1) + JS id: array detection (Strategy 2). HUB-002's premise was wrong — the validator is built; the gap was that findings weren't being surfaced/triaged.

Fresh HEUR-025 scan at marathon-tick-3 found 177 findings platform-wide (none in TREASURE_MAP because that file last updated 2026-04-13, before the recent EduScan additions). Distribution:
  - 80 Strategy 1 (high-precision): network-plus 53, server-plus 20, security-plus 3, isc2-cc 2, python-for-it 1, cmmc 1
  - 97 Strategy 2 (loose JS id: match): clh 31, dark-arts 12, python-engineering 12, script/linux 12, shield 6, etc. — mixed real bugs + CATEGORIES false positives

Action taken (commit 721c9fb4):
  - Built `_tools/reports/heur-025-fix-strategy1.js` — bulk-apply script with 7 safety checks (parse message, resolve target, check existence, single-match required, no newKey-collision, dual-target detection, dry-run mode).
  - Nancy review: PROCEED with grep precondition (no instructor admin pages reference old keys). Verified clean.
  - Applied 78 of 80 Strategy 1 fixes (1 dual-target file excluded: cloud/wsa/m10-group-policy/cloud-presentation.module.html, where 2 hub cards point at same file — operator decision needed).
  - Verification: HEUR-025 platform-wide 177 -> 98 (Strategy 1 80 -> 2 expected residual, Strategy 2 97 -> 96).

Follow-ups tracked separately:
  - Strategy 2 triage (97 findings, mostly CATEGORIES FPs but 30-50 real bugs likely): see new task #81.
  - m10 dual-target architectural decision: backlog for cloud/server-plus operator review.
  - HEUR-025 validator refinement (skip CATEGORIES arrays in Strategy 2): pending Nancy + decision-protocol; the rule-not-rule-clearing line is delicate (see feedback memory).

--- 2026-05-08 STRATEGY 2 DEEP TRIAGE (97 findings → ALL RUNTIME FALSE POSITIVES) ---

Deep-investigated each hub's actual completion-tracking mechanism:

  - dark-arts (10 findings): Hub uses custom `${HOUSE_ID}_${moduleId}_completed` localStorage key, NOT ModuleProgress. Files write to BOTH the custom format (correct, matches hub) AND ModuleProgress (long-key, validator detects). ModuleProgress write is dead code at runtime. FP.

  - script/courses/clh (31 findings): Hub has IN-PAGE migration logic at lines 433-473 that reads `script-clh-NNN-intro` and `script-clh-NNN-lab` legacy keys and migrates them to canonical `clh-NNN`. Files writing the legacy keys are migrated forward by hub on every page load. Validator can't see migration logic; its complaint is technically true but functionally moot. FP.

  - script/linux (12 findings): Hub uses `CHAPTERS = [{id: 'ch01', presId: 'script-linux-la-ch01-intro', labId: 'script-linux-la-ch01-intro-lab'}]`. The id is just a chapter index. Completion check uses `presId` and `labId` (lines 618-619) which DO match what files write. Validator only matched on `id:` and missed the presId/labId structure. FP.

  - code/modules/python-engineering (12 findings): Hub uses custom PYEProgress library with short keys (`ch01`, `ch02`, etc.) — matches what files write VIA `PYEProgress.markModuleComplete('ch03')`. Files ALSO call `ModuleProgress.complete()` with longer keys (cross-system compatibility); the ModuleProgress write is dual-redundant. FP.

  - root-hub CATEGORIES (27 across shield/script/ai/cloud/web/forge/code/eye/key): JS `id:` values are navigation pill labels, not completion-tracking keys. No hub completion-check uses them. FP.

  - Other 5 (armory 2, dark-arts 2, script 1): same bespoke-progress pattern.

**Verdict**: HEUR-025 Strategy 2 (loose JS `id:` array match) is a STRUCTURAL FALSE-POSITIVE GENERATOR for hubs with bespoke progress systems. 97/97 findings are runtime noise.

**Recommendation**: HEUR-025 Strategy 2 should be refined to ONLY fire when (a) the hub explicitly calls `ModuleProgress.isCompleted()` with the JS-array id, AND (b) the linked target file's `ModuleProgress.complete()` write-key differs. Without that contextual check, Strategy 2 is anti-signal.

**Action**: Strategy 2 findings are a WAIT — don't fix, don't bulk-modify. The validator change should happen in a separate Nancy-reviewed PR. For now, treat these 97 findings as triaged-and-acknowledged-FPs in the operator dashboard.

No file edits this round. Triage data preserved at `_tools/reports/heur-025-strategy2-triage-2026-05-08.json`.

--- 2026-05-08 NANCY REVIEW REVERSED THE FP DETERMINATION ---

Proposed a Strategy 2 severity demotion (HIGH -> LOW) on the basis of '97/97 are runtime FPs.' Nancy PAUSE with two specific verification gates that I had skipped.

Gate 1 (CLH new file write-pattern): Checked recent CLH module files (clh-020 through clh-028, all from late April 2026 builds). EVERY one calls `ModuleProgress.complete('script', 'script-clh-NNN-intro', ...)` — the legacy format. The migration shim at hub lines 433-473 is masking AN ONGOING WRITE-PATTERN MISMATCH, not just preserving legacy student data. The CLH file template was never updated to write canonical clh-NNN keys. 31 CLH findings represent real architectural drift.

Gate 2 (python-engineering ModuleProgress consumption): Files write 'pye-chN' keys via ModuleProgress.complete (12 calls confirmed across chapters 02-10 + capstone + midterm). Hub does NOT call ModuleProgress.isCompleted (zero hits) — uses PYEProgress.getStatus for display. BUT: ModuleProgress writes go to localStorage `hexworth_progress` which is ALSO consumed by XPCalculator + leaderboards + instructor dashboard (FirestoreManager.js sync paths). 'Redundant' is wrong — the ModuleProgress write is the live XP path even though hub display uses PYEProgress.

Verdict: '97/97 are runtime FPs' was too aggressive. Real status:
  - Pure FPs: 27 CATEGORIES navigation pills (JS id never participates in any completion mechanism)
  - Runtime-workaround-by-shim (architectural drift): 31 CLH (shim-masked write-pattern bug)
  - Multi-system consumption (XP path active): 12 python-engineering + likely some script/linux
  - Mixed runtime status: 27 OTHER (armory + dark-arts + script root)

**Demotion ABANDONED.** Current HIGH severity is appropriate signal — these findings represent real architectural drift even when runtime-masked. Demoting would have masked CLH ongoing write-pattern bug and python-engineering XP-path drift. This was the rule-change-to-clear-flag temptation that the memory rule warns against.

Lesson logged: when validator-finding triage suggests a FP class, run Nancy verification gates to test the assumption per-hub-class BEFORE proposing severity changes. The FP-class determination needs verified per-hub runtime evidence, not just classification by JS array name.

sprints.title: Resolve nt1-network-troubleshoot storageKey collision (arena vs dispatch duplicate)
sprints.notes:
Surfaced by EduScan validator BOX-042 (_tools/eduscan/box-storage-key-uniqueness.js). Same box dirname (nt1-network-troubleshoot) exists in BOTH _app/arena/boxes/ AND _app/dispatch/boxes/ — both declare storageKey='hexworth_lab_nt1'. Student progress on one corrupts the other (localStorage cross-pollution).

INVESTIGATION (2026-05-23 session): the two files have DIVERGED — they are not pure duplicates. Diff: arena version uses async functions + calls BoxEngine.requestFlagText() (server-delivered flag values); dispatch version is sync and uses static aliases (Mode-2 validateFlag scan). Both reference const NT1Config but the arena hub already calls it with a DIFFERENT storageKey (hexworth_ctf_nt1 — see _app/arena/index.html:1405) — so arena hub's link is already orphaned from the config's declared storageKey.

RECOMMENDED FIX: (a) decide which is canonical (arena vs dispatch) based on which mechanism (async server-delivered vs sync alias-based) is the platform's preferred pattern, (b) rename the non-canonical one's storageKey to e.g. 'hexworth_lab_nt1_arena', (c) update the arena hub link in _app/arena/index.html:1405 to match. Both files are ~95KB and ~95% identical content; full merge would lose the mechanism distinction.

Re-run validator after fix: node _tools/eduscan/box-storage-key-uniqueness.js

sprints.title: Sablier-restart path never re-runs mission seed (mid-mission student gets unseeded box marked ready)
sprints.notes: Found in Nancy review of the launch readiness gate 2026-07-09. lab-manager server.js /launch: the startStoppedContainer restart branch does NOT call missionEngine.runSeed (only the already-running reuse branch does, conditioned on missionId). A student mid-mission whose box idle-stops and restarts gets no re-seed; post-readiness-gate the response even says ready:true. Fix: mirror the reuse branch's idempotent runSeed in the restart branch when session.mission is set. Seeds are contract-idempotent (destructive seeds self-guard), so re-running is safe by design.

sprints.title: Fleet monitoring & alerting — build & verify (Prometheus fix + container crash-loop alerts + ntfy push)
sprints.notes:
Fleet monitoring & alerting BUILT + VERIFIED 2026-07-11 (response to the ~80-day silent redis crash-loop incident). What was done:
- Root cause + fix: Prometheus had been detached from its Docker network ~9 days (Cockpit's systemd socket claimed host port 9090); remapped Prometheus to host 9091, all fleet targets (bc1/bc2/neon) back up.
- docker-restart-exporter.py: container RestartCount/health from the Docker API (cAdvisor is broken on neon's containerd image store — Storage Driver overlayfs).
- 6 alert rules: ContainerCrashLooping / ContainerRestarting / ContainerUnhealthy / ScrapeTargetDown (self-reports blindness) / DiskAlmostFull / HostMemoryHigh.
- Alertmanager + webhook-ntfy formatting relay + self-hosted ntfy (Tailscale-bound); Prometheus scrapes itself + Alertmanager (watches the watcher).
- Verified end-to-end: a real crash-looping container fired a readable push in minutes. Nancy-reviewed; promtool/amtool validated before apply.
- DR mirror in repo _tools/monitoring/ (was live-only on neon); runbook _docs/operations/monitoring-alerting.md; admin KBA Confluence page 43417601; memory reference_monitoring_alerting.
Remaining follow-on = MON-2 (external dead-man's-switch).

sprints.title: External dead-man's-switch: off-neon watcher that alerts if neon monitoring goes dark
sprints.notes:
EXTERNAL DEAD-MAN'S-SWITCH for the neon monitoring stack. Closes the one known gap in the 2026-07-10 alerting build: the alerter (Prometheus/Alertmanager/ntfy) runs ON neon, so if neon itself dies the alerting dies silently with it. Need an OFF-neon watcher that screams if neon's monitoring goes dark.

CONTEXT / READ FIRST: _docs/operations/monitoring-alerting.md (runbook), memory reference_monitoring_alerting.md, and the KBA 'Hexworth Monitoring & Alerting'. Stack lives at /home/eq/hexworth-monitoring on neon, mirrored in repo _tools/monitoring/. neon Tailscale IP 100.65.122.90. Prometheus host 9091, Alertmanager 100.65.122.90:9093, ntfy 100.65.122.90:8090 topic hexworth-alerts.

DESIGN (pre-decided, account-free — do NOT stop to ask): cross-host heartbeat from bc1. The primary ntfy is on neon and dies with it, so the dead-man delivery path must NOT traverse neon. Approach:
1. Stand up a SECOND tiny ntfy on bc1 (distinct compose project, e.g. /home/eq/hexworth-deadman on bc1), topic hexworth-deadman, bound to bc1's Tailscale interface (get bc1 IP via `tailscale ip -4` on bc1; verify 8090 free on bc1 first — pick another port if taken).
2. Install a checker cron on bc1 (every 5 min): curl neon Prometheus http://100.65.122.90:9091/-/healthy AND Alertmanager http://100.65.122.90:9093/-/healthy. Keep a counter file; on 3 consecutive failures push a CRITICAL message to bc1's hexworth-deadman ntfy ('neon monitoring DOWN — <which endpoint> unreachable'). On recovery push a resolved message and reset the counter.
3. (Stretch, optional) symmetry: have neon's stack also probe bc1/bc2 liveness so a dead bc1 is caught too. Not required for acceptance.
ALTERNATIVE (note only, do not build unless owner later asks): healthchecks.io SaaS is zero-maintenance and fully external, but needs an owner account/API key — that's why the self-hosted cross-check is the default.

FILES: add under repo mirror _tools/monitoring/deadman/ : check-peer.sh (the cron script, dead-simple curl+counter, pure POSIX sh), deadman-compose.yml (bc1 second-ntfy), and a README. git add -f (tools is gitignored). Update _docs/operations/monitoring-alerting.md 'follow-ups' section to mark this done + how to operate. Update the KBA with the second (deadman) subscription steps.

OWNER ACTION TO RECORD (not blocking the build): Frank subscribes his S25 to a SECOND ntfy subscription — server http://<bc1-tailscale-ip>:8090 topic hexworth-deadman. Document in KBA; leave a note in the completion summary so the operator does it.

ACCEPTANCE (must self-verify unsupervised, no questions):
a) bc1 second-ntfy up + reachable on bc1 Tailscale interface (curl 200). Checker cron installed and running; healthy state produces NO alert.
b) FAILOVER TEST with neon monitoring fully stopped: on neon `docker stop prometheus alertmanager`. Within ~15 min bc1 detects 3 consecutive failures and pushes 'neon monitoring DOWN' to hexworth-deadman. Poll bc1 ntfy (http://<bc1-ip>:8090/hexworth-deadman/json?poll=1) and CONFIRM the message landed WHILE neon monitoring was down — this proves the delivery path does not depend on neon. Then `docker start prometheus alertmanager` on neon; confirm recovery/resolved message.
c) No student sandbox containers on bc1 disturbed (lab-manager caveat — use a distinct compose project; never `docker compose down` the lab-manager stack).

GOTCHAS: Zscaler can block Tailscale in some contexts (see reference_sandbox_infrastructure) — bc1->neon is server-to-server over the tailnet, should be fine, but if curl to 100.65.122.90 fails from bc1, diagnose the route before assuming neon is down. Keep the checker idempotent and quiet on success. Do NOT publish anything to production Firebase — this is self-hosted infra only, no deploy gate applies.

sprints.title: Integrity: submission rate limit has TWO independent bypasses
sprints.notes: DEPLOYED 2026-08-29. Nancy APPROVED after verifying empirically, not by reading: 20 concurrent submissions from one user gave accepted=8 throttled=12 storedCount=8, so no double-count under real retry contention and the exactly-1-of-5 result is Firestore OCC rather than luck. A/B: pre-fix 12/12 accepted and 5/5 raced; fixed 8+4 throttled and exactly 1 of 5. Both her asks applied before deploy: the 'sliding window' comment corrected to FIXED (she proved a ~16-request boundary burst by rewinding windowStart), and exhausted transaction retries now map to resource-exhausted instead of a raw internal. RESIDUALS she found, low severity: budget is spent before the challenge-exists check, so a stale challengeId burns a slot; and there is no admin reset path for rateLimits (60s max wait, no UI renders it).

sprints.title: Secrecy: hidden challenges are fully readable pre-auth -- reveal is cosmetic
sprints.notes: 'visible' is enforced for SCORING in ctfSubmitFlag (functions/index.js:7018) -- that half was fixed after a proven exploit -- but it appears NOWHERE in firestore.rules, and challenges are 'allow read: if true'. An unrevealed challenge's title, description, hints, flagHash and flagSalt are readable by anyone, unauthenticated. Phased reveal is presentation-only. Fix: gate challenge reads on visible, or accept it and document reveal as cosmetic -- but the code and the rules should stop implying different things. Taskboard #319.

sprints.title: Secrecy: console's own example flags are the crackable shape
sprints.notes: flagHash AND flagSalt both sit on a world-readable doc, so the salt was never secret and only the flag's entropy matters. Mallory recovered a two-word flag in 171,806 attempts / 125ms and measured 1.52M hashes/sec on ONE core -- a full two-word dictionary space is ~1 hour on CPU, ~1 second on a consumer GPU. The console's own examples (HEX{view_source_is_your_friend} at console.html:4006, guidance at :3931) are exactly that shape. A random 128-bit flag in the same field is safe: this is a flag-AUTHORING problem, not a broken scheme. Fix: change the examples to high-entropy tokens and say why in the admin guidance.

sprints.title: Perf: index team membership instead of scanning all teams per call
sprints.notes: DO NOT DO THIS FIRST -- it is the most tempting item here and the least useful. Both hot-path functions load the ENTIRE teams collection per call to identify the caller (index.js:6959 in ctfSubmitFlag, :7238 in ctfJoinTeam). Measured against the deployed functions: join p50 1.45s at 32 teams, 3.07s at 250, 8.79s at 1000; the scan alone is 69ms at 10 teams and 276ms at 1000. Real, and IRRELEVANT until TOURN-01 raises the ceiling -- at six teams it is invisible. Nothing crashed at any scale tested; the failure mode is latency, not collapse. Fix when capacity moves past ~100 teams: a uid->teamId lookup doc, or the rosterLocks doc already written at join.

sprints.title: deleteTournament orphans subcollections -- now up to 200 team docs, not 6
sprints.notes: Raised by Nancy reviewing TOURN-01. _app/admin/console.html deleteTournament() only does deleteDoc on the tournament doc -- it never removes teams, challenges, submissions or rosterLocks. PRE-EXISTING, but TOURN-01 amplifies the orphan ceiling 33x: a deleted tournament used to strand at most 6 team docs, now up to 200. Realistic trigger: an admin deletes a mis-configured tournament and recreates it before a class. Harmless to the new tournament (addDoc gives a fresh id) but it is unbounded Firestore debris with no cleanup path. Fix: recursive delete of the subcollections, ideally in a Cloud Function so it is not 200+ client round trips. Note _tools/tournament/benchmark-tournament.js --cleanup already implements exactly this paging-delete pattern and can be lifted.

sprints.title: Rate limit spends budget before the challenge-exists check
sprints.notes: Nancy, reviewing TOURN-04. The throttle transaction runs at step 4, BEFORE the challenge is loaded at step 5, so a typo'd or stale challengeId consumes real per-user budget for a request that can never succeed. She PROVED it: 8 submissions to nonexistent challenge ids all failed downstream, yet the stored count still reached 8. Self-inflicted and per-uid, not exploitable against another user, which is why it is low severity. Fix: check challenge existence before committing the rate-limit transaction (already-solved is correctly checked first already). SECOND ITEM, same area: there is no admin reset path for rateLimits/* -- it is denied to every client and no Cloud Function clears it, so a mis-tuned limit has no remedy faster than waiting out the 60s window. Low stakes at 60s, worth knowing.
